explanation: The engine did not reach its expected operating temperature within the expected time. This is a warm-up rationality fault: the ECU watches coolant temperature rise against a model, not a single sensor reading.

repairs.label: Replace thermostat and gasket
repairs.verification: Refill and bleed the cooling system, then confirm the warm-up curve reaches 85–95 °C within 10 minutes of driving.

repairs.label: Replace coolant temperature sensor
repairs.verification: Rescan; confirm the warm-up curve looks plausible and P0128 stays clear.

repairs.label: Top up coolant and inspect for leaks
repairs.verification: With the engine cold, bring the reservoir to the MAX mark and re-check the level after a week of driving.

safety.stop_message: Overheating or severe coolant loss: stop the engine and seek professional service.

conditions.note: Cold start, then normal driving. One coolant-temperature sample every 10 s for 10 minutes; the app derives the 10-minute reading, the total rise, and whether the curve fluctuates.

tests.question: From a cold start, log coolant temperature (PID 05) over the first 10 minutes of driving. What does the curve show?

level_ok.label: Level between MIN and MAX, no visible leaks

tests.question: With the engine cold, is the coolant level in the reservoir clearly below the MIN mark, or are there visible leaks?

title: Coolant temperature below thermostat regulating temperature
